Parse and validate identifiers

Source: R/parse.R
id_parse.Rd

id_parse() turns text into a zuid vector of one format, holding each element's canonical text. id_valid() is the vectorised predicate.

Usage

id_parse(
  x,
  format = NULL,
  form = NULL,
  layout = NULL,
  level = c("structure", "syntax", "strict"),
  strict = FALSE
)

id_valid(
  x,
  format,
  form = NULL,
  layout = NULL,
  level = c("structure", "syntax", "strict")
)

Arguments

x

A character vector.

format

The format, such as "uuid". See id_formats(). Required for now; detecting it from x is not available yet.

form

A text form of format, or NULL for its canonical text.

layout

Reserved for formats that need a layout.

level

The validation level elements must reach.

strict

If TRUE, an element that fails level is an error of class zuid_parse_error. If FALSE, it becomes NA.

Value

id_parse(): a zuid vector, the same length as x, with NA where an element is missing or fails level. id_valid(): a logical vector, NA where x is.

Details

Validation is cumulative over three levels:

  • "syntax": the alphabet, length, case rule and separators of the form.

  • "structure": syntax, and the value's own rules. For a UUID, the variant bits are the RFC's (10), except for the nil and max UUIDs.

  • "strict": structure, and the value is one its specification defines. For a UUID, the version is 1 to 8 (or nil or max), and a time field is no later than now plus the option zuid.time_tolerance (seconds, one day by default).

A UUID's canonical text is lowercase and hyphenated. On input, either case is accepted, and form selects another of the RFC 9562 text forms: "compact" (32 hex digits), "urn" (urn:uuid: prefix), "braced" or "uppercase", or one of the encodings of id_encode() over the 16 bytes, such as "base32", "base58" or "words".

A ULID is 26 Crockford base32 characters, uppercase, either case on input, starting 0 to 7. A TypeID is a lowercase prefix, _ and 26 lowercase Crockford characters, or the 26 alone; strict asks what it asks of the UUID. A UPID is four prefix characters, _ and 22 lowercase characters, as the reference writes them; strict asks for the current version. SCRU128 is 25 base36 characters and SCRU64 12, lowercase, either case on input; their reserved timestamps (the first and the last) pass "syntax" only. A KSUID is 27 base62 characters, case-sensitive, at most aWgEPTl1tmebfsQzFP4bxwgy80V. Strict also asks that a time is no later than now plus the tolerance. These formats have one text form each.

Examples

x <- id_parse("018F6B1C-2D3E-7A4B-8C5D-6E7F8091A2B3", "uuid")
x
#> <zuid_uuid[1]>
#> [1] 018f6b1c-2d3e-7a4b-8c5d-6e7f8091a2b3
id_valid(c("018f6b1c-2d3e-7a4b-8c5d-6e7f8091a2b3", "nope"), "uuid")
#> [1]  TRUE FALSE
id_parse("{018f6b1c-2d3e-7a4b-8c5d-6e7f8091a2b3}", "uuid", form = "braced")
#> <zuid_uuid[1]>
#> [1] 018f6b1c-2d3e-7a4b-8c5d-6e7f8091a2b3
